q-23396.name: Question 1
q-23396.problem: If $m∠A=(5x+16)^{∘}$ and $m∠B=(x+8)^{∘},$ find a value of $x$ that satisfies $\operatorname{cot}⁡A=\operatorname{tan}⁡B.$  Suppose that both $∠A$ and $∠B$ are acute.
q-23396.worked_solution:
If both angles are acute and $\operatorname{cot}⁡A=\operatorname{tan}⁡B,$ then the angles $∠A$ and $∠B$ must be complementary, and we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(5x+16)^{∘}+(x+8)^{∘} & ={90}^{∘} \\ (6x+24)^{∘} & ={90}^{∘} \\ 6x+24 & =90 \\ 6x & =66 \\ x & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

If m∠A=(5x+16)∘ and m∠B=(x+8)∘, find a value of x that satisfies cot⁡A=tan⁡B. Suppose that both ∠A and ∠B are acute.

a
7
b
13
c
−2
d
−4
e
11
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If both angles are acute and cot⁡A=tan⁡B, then the angles ∠A and ∠B must be complementary, and we have

(5x+16)∘+(x+8)∘=90∘(6x+24)∘=90∘6x+24=906x=66x=11.

q-54180.name: Question 2
q-54180.problem: Express $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta +{31}^{∘})$ as a cofunction of a complementary angle.
q-54180.worked_solution:
We know that the cofunction of $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ is $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and the angle complementary to $\theta +{31}^{∘}$ is 

$$
{90}^{∘}-(\theta +{31}^{∘})={90}^{∘}-\theta -{31}^{∘}={59}^{∘}-\theta .
$$

So we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta +{31}^{∘})=\operatorname{sin}⁡({90}^{∘}-(\theta +{31}^{∘}))=\operatorname{sin}⁡({59}^{∘}-\theta ).
$$

q-54180.html:
Question 2
?

Express cos⁡(θ+31∘) as a cofunction of a complementary angle.

a
sin⁡(31∘−θ)
b
sec⁡(31∘−θ)
c
sec⁡(59∘−θ)
d
tan⁡(59∘−θ)
e
sin⁡(59∘−θ)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We know that the cofunction of cos⁡θ is sin⁡θ, and the angle complementary to θ+31∘ is 90∘−(θ+31∘)=90∘−θ−31∘=59∘−θ. So we have

cos⁡(θ+31∘)=sin⁡(90∘−(θ+31∘))=sin⁡(59∘−θ).

q-67541.name: Question 3
q-67541.problem: Determine a value of $x$ satisfying the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡{51}^{∘}=\operatorname{cot}⁡x.$
q-67541.worked_solution:
Since the tangent of an angle equals the cotangent of its complement, we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡{51}^{∘}=\operatorname{cot}⁡({90}^{∘}-{51}^{∘})=\operatorname{cot}⁡{39}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, $x={39}^{∘}$ satisfies the given equation.

q-121635.name: Question 4
q-121635.problem: Express $\operatorname{csc}⁡({52}^{∘}-\theta )$ as a cofunction of a complementary angle.
q-121635.worked_solution:
We know that the cofunction of $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta $ is $\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta ,$ and the angle complementary to ${52}^{∘}-\theta $ is 

$$
{90}^{∘}-({52}^{∘}-\theta )={90}^{∘}-{52}^{∘}+\theta =\theta +{38}^{∘}.
$$

 

 So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡({52}^{∘}-\theta )=\operatorname{sec}⁡({90}^{∘}-({52}^{∘}-\theta ))=\operatorname{sec}⁡(\theta +{38}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

q-121635.html:
Question 4
?

Express csc⁡(52∘−θ) as a cofunction of a complementary angle.

a
cot⁡(θ+38∘)
b
tan⁡(38∘−θ)
c
 sec⁡(θ+38∘)
d
 sin⁡(38∘−θ)
e
 sec⁡(38∘−θ)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We know that the cofunction of csc⁡θ is sec⁡θ, and the angle complementary to 52∘−θ is 90∘−(52∘−θ)=90∘−52∘+θ=θ+38∘.

So we have

csc⁡(52∘−θ)=sec⁡(90∘−(52∘−θ))=sec⁡(θ+38∘).
